ordered_diagnoses: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of depressor anguli oris

s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital facial asymmetry with abnormal lower lip movement
salient_findings: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
key_facts: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
Developmental milestones are appropriate for age
Magnetic resonance imaging of the temporal bones and internal auditory canals is normal
Auditory brainstem response test reveals normal hearing pathways

differentials: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of depressor anguli oris
per_call: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of depressor anguli oris

shortlist: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of depressor anguli oris

shortlist.label: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of depressor anguli oris
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the specific symptom of right lower lip deviation during smiling or crying

shortlist.label: Asymmetric crying face syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by asymmetric facial movement during crying, matching the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Hemifacial microsomia
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause facial asymmetry, although the patient's symmetric facial movement at rest reduces its likelihood

shortlist.label: Moebius syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Involves facial paralysis, but the patient's intact facial functions except for the specific lip deviation make it less likely

shortlist.label: Congenital lower lip pits
shortlist.why_kept: Could be associated with lower lip abnormalities, but the primary symptom here is the deviation during smiling or crying

raw.rationale: The key fact that the right lower lip deviates inward when the child smiles or cries, with otherwise symmetric facial movement, is most consistent with asymmetric crying face syndrome.

rejected.label: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of depressor anguli oris
rejected.why: While this could explain the lip deviation, it is less specific to the crying or smiling actions described

rejected.label: Hemifacial microsomia
rejected.why: This condition typically involves more extensive facial anomalies, not just lip deviation

rejected.label: Moebius syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves paralysis of the facial nerve, which is not indicated here as other facial functions are intact

rejected.label: Congenital lower lip pits
rejected.why: This condition involves physical pits in the lower lip, not mentioned in the case description
